stages.name: Beyond the Punic world
stages.desc: Peoples and coasts with little contact with Ebusus or Carthage

stages.name: Phoenician outposts
stages.desc: Early trading settlements founded by Phoenicians from the East

stages.name: Trading coasts
stages.desc: Ports where Ebusitan amphorae and Punic goods are found

stages.name: Mercenary grounds
stages.desc: Lands where Carthage recruits slingers, infantry and horsemen

stages.name: Punic territory
stages.desc: Land ruled from Carthage, or its own home ground

stages.name: Roman-held
stages.desc: Coasts and islands taken by Rome

states.name: France
timeline: Celtic and Ligurian peoples on the Gulf of Lion
Greeks from Phocaea found Massalia, a rival to Punic trade
Ebusitan and Punic amphorae appear in the native ports of Roussillon and Languedoc
Hannibal marches through southern Gaul and recruits Gallic warriors

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Phoenician traders at Lixus and on the island of Mogador
Lixus and the ports of the Strait trade within the Punic world

states.name: Spain
timeline: Phoenician colonies at Gadir and Malaka; settlers reach Ibiza's south coast at Sa Caleta
Sa Caleta is abandoned; the settlers gather at the harbour of Ibiza town
Iberian mercenaries fight for Carthage at Himera; Ebusitan amphorae spread along the coast
Balearic slingers serve in Carthage's army at Akragas, in Sicily
Hamilcar Barca lands at Gadir and begins the Carthaginian conquest of the south
Hasdrubal founds Carthago Nova, the capital of Punic Spain
A Roman fleet raids Ebusus but fails to take the town
After Ilipa, Rome holds the mainland; Mago sails away by way of Ebusus

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, founded by Tyre in 814 BC by tradition, sends settlers to Ebusus
Under Mago and his heirs Carthage becomes the leading power of the West
Agathocles of Syracuse invades Carthage's African homeland
Unpaid mercenaries revolt; the Mercenary War rages around Carthage

states.name: Italy
timeline: Phoenician towns in western Sicily and Sardinia: Motya, Tharros, Nora, Sulcis
Carthage's army at Himera includes Ligurians, Sardinians and Corsicans
Carthage returns to Sicily with Campanian mercenaries and destroys Selinus
The First Punic War begins over Messana, in Sicily
After the Aegates Islands, Sicily becomes Rome's first province
Rome seizes Sardinia during Carthage's war with its mercenaries

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Numidian and Moorish peoples; a few Phoenician anchorages on the coast
Punic harbour towns such as Iol, Icosium and Hippo trade in Carthage's network
Numidian horsemen serve in Carthage's armies
The Numidian prince Masinissa turns to Rome

states.name: Malta
timeline: Phoenician settlers worship at the sanctuary of Tas-Silġ
Malta passes under Carthage's control
The consul Tiberius Sempronius Longus takes Malta

events.title: Ebusus founded
events.text: Diodorus dates the settling of Ebusus to 160 years after Carthage's founding, in 654 BC.

events.title: Sa Caleta
events.text: Phoenicians from southern Spain build a stone village on a headland of Ibiza's south coast.

events.title: Mogador
events.text: Phoenician traders camp on an island off the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

events.title: Tharros
events.text: Phoenician Tharros flourishes on the west coast of Sardinia.

events.title: Puig des Molins
events.text: The first cremation burials are made on the hill of windmills beside Ibiza town.

events.title: Massalia
events.text: Greeks from Phocaea found Massalia, the future Marseille.

events.title: Sa Caleta abandoned
events.text: The south-coast village is left peacefully; its people move to Ibiza town's harbour.

events.title: Carthage takes Malta
events.text: Malta and its sanctuary of Tas-Silġ come under Carthage.

events.title: Carthage leads
events.text: With Tyre humbled by Babylon, Carthage takes the lead of the Phoenician West.

events.title: Battle of Alalia
events.text: Carthaginian and Etruscan fleets fight Phocaean Greeks off Corsica.

events.title: Treaty with Rome
events.text: Carthage and the young Roman Republic sign their first treaty.

events.title: Hanno's voyage
events.text: A Carthaginian fleet sails past Lixus down Africa's Atlantic coast.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.text: Carthage's army of Iberians, Ligurians and Sardinians is crushed by the Greeks of Sicily.

events.title: Island farms
events.text: Farmsteads such as Ses Païsses de Cala d'Hort spread wine and olive growing across Ibiza.

events.title: Amphorae to Menorca
events.text: Ebusitan amphorae reach Menorca in great numbers.

events.title: Selinus destroyed
events.text: A Carthaginian army with Campanian mercenaries sacks the Greek city of Selinus.

events.title: Slingers at Akragas
events.text: Balearic slingers serve in the Carthaginian siege of Akragas.

events.title: Es Culleram
events.text: A cave in the north of Ibiza becomes a sanctuary of the goddess Tanit.

events.title: Motya falls
events.text: Dionysius of Syracuse storms the Phoenician island town of Motya.

events.title: The mint of Ebusus
events.text: Ebusus strikes its own coins, stamped with the dwarf god Bes.

events.title: Second treaty
events.text: A new treaty keeps Roman traders out of Carthage's western waters.

events.title: Na Guardis
events.text: Ebusitan traders work from an islet off southern Mallorca.

events.title: Agathocles
events.text: The tyrant of Syracuse lands in Africa and threatens Carthage itself.

events.title: Purple and salt
events.text: Murex shells at Pou des Lleó point to purple dyeing on Ibiza's east coast.

events.title: First Punic War
events.text: Rome and Carthage go to war over Messana in Sicily.

events.title: Battle of Mylae
events.text: Rome's new fleet wins its first great sea battle.

events.title: Aegates Islands
events.text: Carthage's fleet is destroyed; it gives up Sicily.

events.title: Mercenary War
events.text: Carthage's unpaid mercenaries revolt in Africa.

events.title: Sardinia lost
events.text: Rome seizes Sardinia while Carthage is weak.

events.title: Hamilcar in Spain
events.text: Hamilcar Barca lands at Gadir to build a new empire in Iberia.

events.title: Carthago Nova
events.text: Hasdrubal founds a new Carthage on Spain's south-east coast.

events.title: Siege of Saguntum
events.text: Hannibal besieges Saguntum, Rome's ally.

events.title: Hannibal's march
events.text: Hannibal crosses the Rhône on his way to the Alps and Italy.

events.title: Rome takes Malta
events.text: The Carthaginian garrison of Malta surrenders to a Roman consul.

events.title: Battle of the Ebro
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio's fleet routs the Carthaginian squadron at the Ebro mouth.

events.title: Ebusus holds
events.text: Scipio's fleet besieges Ebusus for two days, burns the countryside, but cannot take the town.

events.title: Balearic envoys
events.text: Envoys from the Balearic Islands come to Scipio to ask for peace.

events.title: Battle of Cannae
events.text: Balearic slingers open Hannibal's greatest victory.

events.title: Scipios killed
events.text: Both Roman commanders in Spain are defeated and killed.

events.title: Carthago Nova falls
events.text: Publius Scipio storms the capital of Punic Spain.

events.title: Battle of Ilipa
events.text: Scipio breaks the last Carthaginian army in Spain.

events.title: Mago at Ebusus
events.text: Shut out of Gadir, Mago is welcomed at Ebusus and given food, arms and young men.

events.title: Mago in Menorca
events.text: Driven from Mallorca by slingers, Mago winters at the harbour that bears his name, Mahón.

chartNote: Share of the area of seven of today's countries (Spain, France, Italy, Malta, Tunisia, Algeria and Morocco, clipped to the map), by their main relationship with the Punic world. Regions are today's boundaries, and each country takes one colour although the ancient contacts were mostly coastal and overlapped; dates are turning points, many of them approximate.
